name: Alt-right
summary: A loose, largely online white-nationalist and identitarian movement that emerged around 2008-2016, holding that white (European) identity is under attack from multiculturalism, egalitarianism and liberal elites. It favours racial separation or an ethnostate, sharply restricted immigration, nationalism and anti-globalism, and it rejects Enlightenment equality and the conservative establishment. Economics is a minor concern, with protectionist leanings.
scope: The mainstream white-nationalist 'Alternative Right' of 2010-2017 associated with Richard Spencer, Greg Johnson and Jared Taylor, with the Daily Stormer as its harder edge. It excludes the 'alt-lite' civic-nationalist wing and the paleoconservatism it grew from. Because the movement had no program, answers on economics and social issues are mostly low-confidence inferences.

regulate-corporations.rationale: No stated line; anti-'globalist' hostility to big business is offset by indifference to economics.

cut-welfare.rationale: Not a focus; welfare is framed by race and citizenship rather than dependency.

worker-ownership.rationale: Inferred: left-economic redistribution is not part of the movement and it rejects socialism.

surveillance-ok.rationale: No stated position; anti-establishment distrust and security concerns pull opposite ways.

legalize-drugs.rationale: No shared position among adherents; the sources do not address this issue, so the answer is inferred.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Members invoke free speech to argue their views must be heard and see speech limits as authoritarian.

strong-leader.rationale: Anglin is reported to want authoritarian government, and Johnson is openly elitist; Trump was admired as a champion.

state-harmful.rationale: Spencer wants a state, an ethnostate, to secure a people; the movement is not anti-statist.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred from the right-wing, anti-liberal orientation.

traditional-family.rationale: Spencer wants women returned to childbearer and homemaker roles; the movement is anti-feminist.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Members show far less interest in homosexuality than US conservatives; some see it as immoral, others are tolerant.

abortion-legal.rationale: Spencer backs legal abortion on racial grounds while others oppose it; no common line.

more-religion-public.rationale: The movement is broadly secular, though some prize Christian heritage.

notes: The movement had no formal program and splintered after Charlottesville (2017). Strands differ on Jews, Christianity, and an ethnostate versus a white-majority nation. Only one primary source (speech excerpts) could be opened; most of the primary writings were inaccessible.
